\chapter{Communication Complexity — Func Inner Product}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.FuncInnerProduct
\section{Overview}

This module establishes a discrepancy lower bound for the mod-2 inner product function
$\mathrm{IP}_n : \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$.  It shows that every
combinatorial rectangle has discrepancy at most $2^{-n/2}$ under the uniform
distribution, and derives from this a public-coin communication complexity lower bound
via the discrepancy method.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Overlap of two bit-vectors]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.overlap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.overlap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput}
Given two $n$-bit inputs $x, y : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$, $\mathrm{overlap}(x, y)$ is
the \texttt{Finset} of coordinates $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ on which both $x$ and $y$
are \texttt{true}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Mod-2 inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}{pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p003-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput}
$\mathrm{innerProduct}(n, x, y) : \mathrm{Bool}$ is the mod-2 inner product of two
$n$-bit vectors $x$ and $y$: it returns \texttt{true} exactly when the number of
coordinates where both inputs are \texttt{true} is odd, i.e.\ when
$\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge y_i) = 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Inner product with the zero vector is false]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_zero_right}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_zero_right}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.zeroInput}
\difficulty{2}
For every $n$-bit Boolean vector $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the mod-$2$ inner product of $x$
with the all-zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ equals $\mathrm{false}$; that is,
$\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge 0) = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform mass of each Boolean input]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.pmf_toReal_eq_two_pow_inv}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.pmf_toReal_eq_two_pow_inv}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.toPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and regard the type of $n$-bit Boolean inputs
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ as a finite probability space, with its associated
probability mass function $p$. Then for every input $x$, the mass assigned to $x$,
viewed as a real number, is
\[
p(x) = \frac{1}{2^{\,n}}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integral as arithmetic average over Boolean inputs]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.integral_eq_average_sum}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.integral_eq_average_sum}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.integral_eq_pmf_sum, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.pmf_toReal_eq_two_pow_inv}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f \colon \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n \to \bbr$ be any real-valued function on the $n$-bit
Boolean inputs. Then, integrating $f$ against the uniform probability measure on the
$2^n$ inputs,
\[
  \int f \;=\; \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x} f(x),
\]
so that the integral equals the arithmetic average of the values $f(x)$ taken over all
$x \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Flipping an active coordinate toggles the mod-2 inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_flipAt_eq_xor}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_flipAt_eq_xor}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.flipAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and let $i$ be a coordinate at which $y_i =
\mathtt{true}$. Write $\langle u, v\rangle = \bigoplus_{j} (u_j \wedge v_j)$ for the
mod-2 inner product of two $n$-bit inputs, and let $x'$ denote the input agreeing with
$x$ at every coordinate except $i$, where $x'_i = \lnot\, x_i$. Then \[ \langle x',
y\rangle = \langle x, y\rangle \oplus \mathtt{true}, \] so negating the $i$-th
coordinate of $x$ flips the value of the inner product.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing Walsh character sum for a nonzero index]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zero_of_exists_true}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zero_of_exists_true}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_flipAt_eq_xor, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign_xor, CommunicationComplexity.flipAt, CommunicationComplexity.flipAt_bijective}
\difficulty{5}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $z$ be an $n$-bit Boolean input that is $\mathrm{true}$ in at
least one coordinate, say $z_i = \mathrm{true}$ for some index $i$. For a Boolean input
$x$, write $\langle x, z\rangle = \bigoplus_{j} (x_j \wedge z_j)$ for their mod-2 inner
product, and let $s(x) \in \{\pm 1\}$ be the sign $+1$ when $\langle x, z\rangle$ is
$\mathrm{false}$ and $-1$ when it is $\mathrm{true}$. Then summing this sign over all
$2^n$ Boolean inputs $x$ gives
\[
  \sum_{x} s(x) = 0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Character sum of the mod-2 inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zeroInput_indicator}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zeroInput_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct_zero_right, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zero_of_exists_true, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.exists_true_of_ne_zeroInput, CommunicationComplexity.zeroInput}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a bit-string $z \in \{0,1\}^n$, and for each $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ let $\langle x,
z\rangle \in \{0,1\}$ denote the mod-2 inner product of $x$ and $z$. Summing the Boolean
sign $(-1)^{\langle x, z\rangle}$ over all $2^n$ inputs $x$ gives
\[
  \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} (-1)^{\langle x, z\rangle}
  \;=\;
\begin{cases} 2^n & \text{if $z$ is the all-zero string,} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Coordinatewise xor of Boolean inputs]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput}
$\mathrm{xorInput}(y, z) : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ is the coordinatewise XOR of $y$
and $z$: $(\mathrm{xorInput}(y, z))_i = y_i \oplus z_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Coordinatewise xor evaluated at a coordinate]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput_apply}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput_apply}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $y, z \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be two $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and
let $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ be a coordinate. Then the $i$-th coordinate of their
coordinatewise xor equals the xor of their individual $i$-th coordinates, namely $y_i
\oplus z_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coordinatewise xor vanishes exactly on equal inputs]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput_eq_zeroInput_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput_eq_zeroInput_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput, CommunicationComplexity.zeroInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $y, z \in \bbf_2^n$ be two $n$-bit Boolean strings, and let $y \oplus z$ denote
their coordinatewise xor, the string whose $i$-th bit is $y_i \oplus z_i$. Then $y
\oplus z$ is the all-zero string if and only if $y = z$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplicativity of the inner-product sign under coordinatewise XOR]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_xorInput}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_xorInput}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign_sum}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n \in \bbn$, and for $u,v \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ write $\langle u, v\rangle \in
\mathrm{Bool}$ for the mod-$2$ inner product, and $s(b) \in \{\pm 1\}$ for the Boolean
sign of $b$ (so $s(\mathrm{false}) = 1$ and $s(\mathrm{true}) = -1$). Then for all $x,
y, z \in \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$,
\[
  s\big(\langle x, y\rangle\big)\cdot s\big(\langle x, z\rangle\big)
  = s\big(\langle x,\, y \oplus z\rangle\big),
\]
where $y \oplus z$ denotes the coordinatewise XOR of $y$ and $z$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Summed Walsh orthogonality for the mod-2 inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_indicator}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_xorInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_eq_zeroInput_indicator, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.xorInput_eq_zeroInput_iff, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{2}
Fix $n \in \bbn$. For a Boolean value $b$, let $\varepsilon(b) \in \{\pm 1\}$ denote its
Boolean sign, equal to $+1$ when $b$ is $\mathrm{false}$ and $-1$ when $b$ is
$\mathrm{true}$; and for $n$-bit Boolean inputs $x, y$, let $\langle x, y\rangle$ denote
their mod-2 inner product (which is $\mathrm{true}$ exactly when the number of
coordinates $i$ with $x_i = y_i = \mathrm{true}$ is odd). Then for any two $n$-bit
Boolean inputs $y$ and $z$,
\[
\sum_{x} \varepsilon\bigl(\langle x, y\rangle\bigr)\,\varepsilon\bigl(\langle x,
z\rangle\bigr)
  = \begin{cases} 2^n & \text{if } y = z, \\ 0 & \text{if } y \neq z, \end{cases}
\]
where the sum ranges over all $2^n$ Boolean inputs $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Idempotence of the 0–1 indicator function]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_sq}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_sq}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput}
\difficulty{2}
Let $B$ be a set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and let $\mathbf{1}_B \colon
(\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \bbr$ be its indicator function, taking the
value $1$ at points of $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then for every $n$-bit Boolean input $y$,
\[ \bigl(\mathbf{1}_B(y)\bigr)^2 = \mathbf{1}_B(y). \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator function bounded by one]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_le_one}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput}
\difficulty{2}
Let $B \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ be a set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and let
$\mathbf{1}_B \colon \mathrm{BoolInput}(n) \to \bbr$ denote its indicator function,
taking the value $1$ on $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then for every $y \in
\mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ one has $\mathbf{1}_B(y) \le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Sum of squared row-sums as a sum over column pairs]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_eq_sum_prod}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_eq_sum_prod}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types and let $f : \alpha \to \beta \to \bbr$. Then
\[
  \sum_{x \in \alpha} \Bigl(\sum_{y \in \beta} f(x,y)\Bigr)^2
  \;=\;
  \sum_{(y,z) \in \beta \times \beta} \; \sum_{x \in \alpha} f(x,y)\, f(x,z).
\]
That is, squaring each row-sum of $f$ and summing over rows yields the same value as
summing, over every ordered pair of columns $(y,z)$, the inner product of those two
columns.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Factoring scalars out of a sum of products]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_mul}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $a, b \in \bbr$ be constants, and let $f, g : \alpha
\to \bbr$ be functions. Then
\[
  \sum_{x : \alpha} (a\, f(x))\,(b\, g(x))
  \;=\; a\, b \sum_{x : \alpha} f(x)\, g(x).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Diagonal collapse of an indexed sum]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_ite_eq_diag}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_ite_eq_diag}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $h \colon \alpha \times
\alpha \to \bbr$ be any function, and let $c \in \bbr$. Summing $h(y,z)$ against the
weight that equals $c$ when $y = z$ and $0$ otherwise, over all ordered pairs, leaves
only the diagonal terms:
\[
\sum_{(y,z)\,\in\,\alpha \times \alpha} h(y,z)\cdot\bigl(\text{$c$ if $y = z$, else
$0$}\bigr)
    \;=\; \sum_{y\,\in\,\alpha} h(y,y)\cdot c.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted orthogonality identity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_of_orthogonal}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_of_orthogonal}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_ite_eq_diag, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_mul_mul, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_eq_sum_prod}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite index sets, and let $\phi : \alpha \times \beta \to
\bbr$ be a real-valued array whose columns are mutually orthogonal with a common squared
length: for a fixed constant $c \in \bbr$,
\[
\sum_{x \in \alpha} \phi(x,y)\,\phi(x,z) = \begin{cases} c & \text{if } y = z,\\ 0 &
\text{if } y \neq z,\end{cases}
\]
for all $y, z \in \beta$. Then for any weights $b : \beta \to \bbr$,
\[
  \sum_{x \in \alpha} \Bigl(\sum_{y \in \beta} b(y)\,\phi(x,y)\Bigr)^{2}
  \;=\; c \sum_{y \in \beta} b(y)^{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parseval identity for mod-2 inner-product characters]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_boolSign_innerProduct}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_boolSign_innerProduct}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_boolSign_innerProduct_mul_eq_indicator, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_of_orthogonal, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{2}
Let $b$ be an arbitrary real-valued function on the set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs. For
two such inputs $x,y$, write $\langle x,y\rangle = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i \wedge y_i)$ for
the number of coordinates on which both are true, so that $(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is
the sign of their mod-2 inner product, equal to $+1$ when $\langle x,y\rangle$ is even
and $-1$ when it is odd. Then
\[
  \sum_{x}\Bigl(\sum_{y} b(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}\Bigr)^2
  \;=\; 2^n \sum_{y} b(y)^2,
\]
where both the inner and outer sums range over all $n$-bit Boolean inputs.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_le_one, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.indicatorOne_sq, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sum_sq_mul_boolSign_innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n \in \bbn$, and identify the set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs with $\{0,1\}^n$. For
$x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, write $\langle x, y\rangle = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge y_i)
\in \{0,1\}$ for their mod-$2$ inner product, so that $(-1)^{\langle x, y\rangle}$
equals $+1$ when $\langle x, y\rangle = 0$ and $-1$ when $\langle x, y\rangle = 1$. Then
for every subset $B \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n}
    \Bigl(\, \sum_{y \in B} (-1)^{\langle x, y\rangle} \Bigr)^{2}
  \;\le\; \bigl(2^{n}\bigr)^{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second-moment bound for the sign-weighted inner-product average]

\difficulty{3}
Let $B \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ be an arbitrary set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, with
indicator $\mathbf 1_B$, and write $\langle x,y\rangle = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge
y_i)$ for the mod-2 inner product of $x,y \in \{0,1\}^n$. Taking $x$ and $y$ to range
independently over $\{0,1\}^n$ under the uniform probability measure,
\[
\int_{x}\left(\int_{y} \mathbf 1_B(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}\right)^{2} \;\le\;
\frac{1}{2^{n}}.
\]
Here $(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is the $\pm 1$ value that is $-1$ when the inner
product is $1$ and $+1$ when it is $0$; equivalently, the average over uniformly random
$x$ of the square of the average over uniformly random $y$ of $\mathbf
1_B(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is at most $2^{-n}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Discrepancy of a rectangle as an iterated integral]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.discrepancy_prod_eq_integral}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.discrepancy_prod_eq_integral}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n$, work over the type $\mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ of $n$-bit Boolean inputs equipped
with a finite probability measure on the product
$\mathrm{BoolInput}(n)\times\mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$, and let $\mathrm{IP}$ denote the
mod-$2$ inner product. For any two subsets $A, B \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$, the
discrepancy of $\mathrm{IP}$ on the combinatorial rectangle $A\times B$ factors as the
iterated integral
\[
  \mathrm{disc}\bigl(\mathrm{IP},\, A\times B\bigr)
= \int_{x} \mathbf{1}_A(x)\left(\int_{y}
\mathbf{1}_B(y)\,\sigma\bigl(\mathrm{IP}(x,y)\bigr)\right),
\]
where $\mathbf{1}_A$ and $\mathbf{1}_B$ are the indicator functions of $A$ and $B$, and
$\sigma$ is the Boolean sign map sending $\mathrm{false}\mapsto 1$ and
$\mathrm{true}\mapsto -1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared discrepancy of an inner-product rectangle]

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.sq_integral_le_integral_sq, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.discrepancy_prod_eq_integral, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.integral_sq_indicator_mul_boolSign_innerProduct_le, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n \in \bbn$ and equip the product $\mathrm{BoolInput}(n) \times
\mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ with its uniform probability measure. For any two sets $A, B
\subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$, the discrepancy of the mod-2 inner product
$\mathrm{IP}_n$ over the combinatorial rectangle $A \times B$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\mathrm{disc}(\mathrm{IP}_n,\, A \times B)\bigr)^2 \;\le\; \frac{1}{2^n}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Rectangle discrepancy bound for the inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.abs_discrepancy_le_of_isRectangle}
\proofsource{raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}{
  pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p004-b002,
  pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p004-b003
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.abs_discrepancy_le_of_isRectangle}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.BoolInput, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.sq_discrepancy_prod_le, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a natural number $n$ and equip the set $\{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ of pairs of
$n$-bit Boolean vectors with the uniform probability measure. Let $\mathrm{IP}_n(x,y) =
\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}(x_i \wedge y_i)$ be the mod-2 inner product. Then for every
rectangle $R \subseteq \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n$ — that is, every set of the form $R =
A \times B$ with $A, B \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ — the discrepancy of $\mathrm{IP}_n$ on $R$
satisfies
\[
  \bigl|\mathrm{disc}(\mathrm{IP}_n, R)\bigr|
  \;\le\;
  \sqrt{\frac{1}{2^{n}}},
\]
where the discrepancy is the expectation over a uniformly random pair $(x,y)$ of
$\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\,\sigma(\mathrm{IP}_n(x,y))$, with $\sigma$ the sign map sending
$\mathrm{false} \mapsto 1$ and $\mathrm{true} \mapsto -1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Public-coin lower bound for the inner product]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.publicCoin_le_communicationComplexity_of_hbound}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}{
  pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p004-b004,
  pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b002,
  pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b001
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.publicCoin_le_communicationComplexity_of_hbound}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.abs_discrepancy_le_of_isRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.InnerProduct.innerProduct, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.lt_communicationComplexity_of_discrepancy_bound}
\difficulty{2}
Let $k, n \in \bbn$ and let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$. If
\[
  2^{k}\,\sqrt{1/2^{n}} \;<\; 1 - 2\varepsilon,
\]
then $k$ is strictly smaller than the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized
communication complexity of the mod-2 inner product function on $n$-bit inputs; that is,
$k < \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}\!\bigl(\mathrm{IP}_{n}\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}
